cards.text: This is a Psalm of David, and he's praying to the LORD. First words out of his mouth, no small talk, no 'hope You're doing well': 'O LORD, hear my prayer.' He asks God to answer him in His faithfulness and His righteousness.
Then David asks God not to bring His servant into judgment. Bold ask, friend, so you KNOW he's got a reason.

cards.question: David asks God not to bring him into judgment. What reason does he give?

answers.text: No one alive is righteous before God
He has never done anything wrong
His enemies should be judged first

cards.text: Then David tells God what's going on. An enemy has been chasing him down, crushing his life to the ground.

cards.question: David says the enemy makes him dwell in darkness. He's like whom?
Inside, David says his spirit grows ___ and his heart is dismayed.

cards.text: Here the psalm turns: David remembers the days of old. You know that move, friend, scrolling WAY back through the old photos on your phone.

cards.question: When David looks back on the days of old, what does he think about?

cards.text: Then David stretches out his hands to God. Not a wave, friend, a full REACH, like me going after the top shelf of sprinkles with nothing but this mustache.

cards.question: David says his soul thirsts for God like a parched land.

cards.text: Then David hits the gas: 'Answer me quickly, O LORD; my spirit fails.' Not 'whenever You get a minute,' not 'let's circle back Monday,' but QUICKLY.

cards.question: David asks God not to hide His face from him. If God does, what does David say he'll be like?

answers.text: Those who descend to the Pit

cards.text: Then David asks for a wake-up call: 'Let me hear Your loving devotion in the morning, for I have put my trust in You.' Now THAT'S an alarm nobody's hitting snooze on.

cards.question: Next, David asks God to teach him the way he should walk.
David asks the LORD to deliver him from his enemies. He says he flees to the ___ for refuge.

cards.text: Then comes the line this psalm is named for: 'Teach me to do Your will, for You are my God.' Friend, that's my prayer before the first tray goes in, and AGAIN after it comes out.

cards.question: David asks God that His good Spirit would lead him on level ground.
David asks the LORD to revive him and bring his soul out of trouble. For whose sake does he ask?

answers.text: For the sake of God's name
For the sake of his family
For the sake of his army

cards.question: In the last line, David asks God to cut off his ___ and calls himself God's ___.

findings.problem: This card asks the baker to guess the wording of David's simile ('like those long since dead'). Nothing earlier points to the dead over a dungeon or the night, since 'dwell in darkness' fits 'Prisoners in a dungeon' just as well. The only way to get it right is luck. This is the same kind of detail-guess as the Psalm 23 'oil' example. Ask about the picture or meaning instead, or give the story card enough context to reason it out.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The question asks who David is like. The wrong answer 'Travelers lost at night' is not a real detail from anywhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The card says 'the line this psalm is named for.' The psalm's own heading is 'A Psalm of David' (Ps 143:1). 'Teach Me to Do Your Will' is the lesson title, not something the text names the psalm. That makes the claim untrue, and it also points at how the lesson is set up. Change it to something like 'Then comes a big one:'.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: All three true or false cards (cards 10, 14 and 17) have True as the right answer. Each one restates the verse almost word for word. A baker who notices this can answer True every time without thinking about the passage.
findings.question: Should true or false cards in a stop mix True and False right answers, or avoid near-verbatim true statements, so the type doesn't become a free pick? The 'No formula' rule covers the order of question types, but not which answer is right.
